title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 74 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 454–456 (Night 74, continuing directly from nights-73), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 74 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. The servant, abused by Ḍawʾ al-Makān but coaxing him gently, brings him to the lady’s house; the stoker follows, anxious that the young man will name him. Ḍawʾ al-Makān is asked to recite, answers that his name and his traces are effaced, and says that of all he has lost the dearest is his sister, at which Nuzhat al-Zamān falls silent. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.l: And when it was the night, the fourth and the seventy,
sentences.i: And when it was the seventy-fourth night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدَأَنَّ الْخَادِمَ قَالَ لِضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ يَا سَيِّدِي إِنِّي أَتَيْتُ إِلَيْكَ فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ ثَلٰثَ مَرَّاتٍ لِأَنَّ سَيِّدَتِي تَدْعُوكَ عِنْدَهَا
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīda anna al-khādima qāla li-ḍawʾi al-makāni yā sayyidī innī atītu ilayka fī hādhihi al-laylati thalātha marrātin li-anna sayyidatī tadʿūka ʿindahā
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that the servant said to Ḍawʾ al-Makān: O my master, I have come to you in this night three times, because my mistress is calling you to be with her.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the servant said to Ḍawʾ al-Makān, “My lord, this is the third time tonight that I have come to you, for my mistress is calling you to her.”
sentences.n: The print runs أن into the word before it (السعيدان, “the happy — that”); it is read as two words. ثلث is the edition’s defective spelling of ثلاث, pointed with the dagger alif.

sentences.t: قَالَ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هَذِهِ الْكَلْبَةُ الَّتِي تَطْلُبُنِي لَعَنَهَا اللَّهُ وَلَعَنَ زَوْجَهَا مَعَهَا وَنَزَلَ فِى الْخَادِمِ شَتْمًا فَمَا قَدَرَ الْخَادِمُ أَنْ يَرُدَّ عَلَيْهِ جَوَابًا
sentences.tr: qāla wa-min ayna hādhihi al-kalbatu allatī taṭlubunī laʿanahā allāhu wa-laʿana zawjahā maʿahā wa-nazala fī al-khādimi shatman fa-mā qadara al-khādimu an yarudda ʿalayhi jawāban
sentences.l: He said: And from where is this bitch who seeks me — God curse her, and curse her husband with her! And he descended upon the servant in cursing, and the servant was not able to return to him an answer.
sentences.i: He said, “And who is this bitch who sends for me? God curse her, and her husband along with her!” And he fell to abusing the servant, who could not answer him back.

sentences.t: لِأَنَّ السِّتَّ أَوْصَتْهُ أَنَّهُ لَا يُؤْذِيهِ وَلَا يُحْضِرُهُ إِلَّا بِمُرَادِهِ هُوَ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَأْتِ مَعَهُ يُعْطِهِ الْمِائَةَ دِينَارٍ فَجَعَلَ الْخَادِمُ يُلَيِّنُ لَهُ الْكَلَامَ
sentences.tr: li-anna al-sitta awṣathu annahu lā yuʾdhīhi wa-lā yuḥḍiruhu illā bi-murādihi huwa fa-in lam yaʾti maʿahu yuʿṭihi al-miʾata dīnārin fa-jaʿala al-khādimu yulayyinu lahu al-kalāma
sentences.l: For the lady had charged him that he not harm him and not bring him except by his own wish; and if he did not come with him, he gives him the hundred dinar. So the servant began softening the speech to him,
sentences.i: For the lady had charged him not to harm the young man, and not to bring him except of his own free will; and if he would not come, the servant was to give him the hundred dinars. So the servant began to speak to him gently,
sentences.n: The grammar of the conditional is loose: the apodosis يعطه is a bare jussive, and the sense is that the hundred dinars the lady gave the servant are the inducement.

sentences.t: وَيَقُولُ لَهُ يَا سَيِّدِي خُذْ هَذِهِ وَاذْهَبْ مَعِي يَا وَلَدِي نَحْنُ مَا أَخْطَأْ نَا مَعَكَ وَلَا جُرْنَا عَلَيْكَ فَالْقَصْدَأَنْ تَصِلَ بِخُطُوَاتِكَ الْكَرِيمَةِ مَعِي إِلَى سَيِّدَتِي تَأْخُذَ مِنْهَا جَوَابًا وَتَرْجِعَ فِي خَيْرٍ وَسَلَامَةٍ وَلَكَ عِنْدَنَا بِشَارَةٌ عَظِيمَةٌ
sentences.tr: wa-yaqūlu lahu yā sayyidī khudh hādhihi wa-idhhab maʿī yā waladī naḥnu mā akhṭaʾ nā maʿaka wa-lā jurnā ʿalayka fa-al-qaṣdaʾan taṣila bi-khuṭuwātika al-karīmati maʿī ilā sayyidatī taʾkhudha minhā jawāban wa-tarjiʿa fī khayrin wa-salāmatin wa-laka ʿindanā bishāratun ʿaẓīmatun
sentences.l: and saying to him: O my master, take this and go with me, O my son; we have not wronged you, and we have not oppressed you; the aim is that you arrive with your generous steps with me to my mistress, you take from her an answer, and you return in good and safety, and for you with us is a great glad-tidings.
sentences.i: saying, “My lord, take this and come with me. My son, we have done you no wrong and no injustice. All that matters is that you favour me with your generous steps to my mistress, take an answer from her, and go back in good health and safety. And there is a great reward waiting for you from us.”
sentences.n: Two printer’s joins: فالقصدأن is فالقصد أن (“the aim is that”) and أخطأ نا is أخطأنا (“we have wronged”, the pronoun split off); both are kept as printed. بشارة is the gift given for good news.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ ذَلِكَ الْكَلَامَ قَامَ وَمَشَى بَيْنَ النَّاسِ وَتَخَطَّا هُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa dhālika al-kalāma qāma wa-mashā bayna al-nāsi wa-takhaṭṭā hum
sentences.l: And when he heard that speech, he rose and walked between the people and stepped-over them,
sentences.i: When he heard this, he got up and walked on through the crowd, stepping past them,
sentences.n: تخطّا هم is printed as two words with a shadda on the ṭāʾ; the split is kept.

sentences.t: وَالْوَقَّادُ مَاشٍ خَلْفَهُ وَنَاظِرٌ إِلَيْهِ وَيَقُولُ فِي نَفْسِهِ يَا خَسَارَةَ شَبَابِهِ فِي غَدٍ يَشْنُقُونَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-al-waqqādu māshin khalfahu wa-nāẓirun ilayhi wa-yaqūlu fī nafsihi yā khasārata shabābihi fī ghadin yashnuqūnahu
sentences.l: and the stoker walking behind him and looking at him, and saying in himself: O the loss of his youth! Tomorrow they hang him.
sentences.i: with the stoker following behind and watching him, and saying to himself, “What a waste of his youth! Tomorrow they will hang him.”

sentences.t: وَمَا زَالَ الْوَقَّادُ مَا شِيًا حَتَّى قَرُبَ مِنْ مَكَانِهِمْ وَهُمْ لَايَرَوْنَهُ وَوَقَفَ وَقَالَ مَا أَخَسَّهُ إِنْ كَانَ يَقُولُ عَلَيَّ هُوَ الَّذِي قَالَ لِي أَنْشِدِ الْأَشْعَارَ
sentences.tr: wa-mā zāla al-waqqādu mā shiyan ḥattā qaruba min makānihim wa-hum lāyarawnahu wa-waqafa wa-qāla mā akhassahu in kāna yaqūlu ʿalayya huwa alladhī qāla lī anshidi al-ashʿāra
sentences.l: And the stoker did not cease walking until he drew near their place, and they not seeing him, and he stopped and said: How base he is, if he says of me: He is the one who said to me, Recite the poems.
sentences.i: The stoker kept on walking until he came near their place, where they could not see him. He stopped and said, “How low he would be, if he were to say of me, ‘He is the one who told me to recite the verses.’”
sentences.n: ما شيا is the print’s split of ماشيا (“walking”). لايرونه is printed as one word. The stoker fears the young man will name him as the one who told him to sing.

sentences.l: This is what was of the matter of the stoker.
sentences.n: مَاكَانَ is printed as one word: “what happened”.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَاكَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ فَابَّهُ مَا زَالَ مَا شِيًا مَعَ الْخَادِمِ حَتَّى وَصَلَ إِلَى الْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mākāna min amri ḍawʾi al-makāni fa-abbahu mā zāla mā shiyan maʿa al-khādimi ḥattā waṣala ilā al-makāni
sentences.l: And as for what was of the matter of Ḍawʾ al-Makān, he did not cease walking with the servant until he reached the place,
sentences.i: As for Ḍawʾ al-Makān, he walked on with the servant until he reached the place,
sentences.n: فابه is a misprint, evidently for فإنه (“for he”); it is pointed as printed.

sentences.t: وَدَخَلَ الْخَادِمُ عَلَى نُزْهَةِ الزَّمَانِ وَقَالَ لَهَا يَا سَيِّدَتِي قَدْ أَحْضَرْتُ لَكِ بِمَنْ تَطْلُبِينَهُ وَهُوَ شَابٌّ حَسَنُ الصُّورَةِ وَعَلَيْهِ آثَارُ النِّعْمَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-dakhala al-khādimu ʿalā nuzhati al-zamāni wa-qāla lahā yā sayyidatī qad aḥḍartu laki bi-man taṭlubīnahu wa-huwa shābbun ḥasanu al-ṣūrati wa-ʿalayhi āthāru al-niʿmati
sentences.l: and the servant entered upon Nuzhat al-Zamān and said to her: O my mistress, I have brought you, with the one you seek; and he is a youth, fair of form, and on him are the traces of ease.
sentences.i: and the servant went in to Nuzhat al-Zamān and said, “My lady, I have brought you the one you were asking for. He is a handsome young man, and he bears the marks of a life of comfort.”
sentences.n: بِمَنْ here belongs to أحضر: the Arabic says “I have brought you with the one you seek”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ ذَلِكَ خَفَقَ قَلْبُهَا وَقَالَتْ دَعْهُ يُنْشِدُ شَيْأً مِنَ الشِّعْرِ حَتَّى أَسْمَعَهُ مِنْ قُرْبٍ وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فَأَسْأَ لَهُ عَنِ اسْمِهِ وَمِنْ أَيِّ الْبِلَادِ هُوَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat dhālika khafaqa qalbuhā wa-qālat daʿhu yunshidu shayʾan mina al-shiʿri ḥattā asmaʿahu min qurbin wa-baʿda dhālika fa-asʾa lahu ʿan ismihi wa-min ayyi al-bilādi huwa
sentences.l: And when she heard that, her heart fluttered, and she said: Leave him to recite something of poetry, until I hear him from near, and after that I ask him about his name and from which of the lands he is.
sentences.i: When she heard this her heart fluttered, and she said, “Let him recite some verse, so that I may hear him close by, and after that I will ask him his name and what country he comes from.”
sentences.n: فاسا له is printed split (فأسأله, “and I ask him”); شيأ is the edition’s own spelling of شيئًا.

sentences.t: فَخَرَجَ الْخَادِمُ إِلَيْهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ قُلْ مَا عِنْدَكَ مِنَ الشِّعْرِ فَإِنَّ السِّتَّ حَاضِرَةٌ بِالْقُرْبِ مِنْكَ تَسْمَعُكَ وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَسْأَلُكَ عَنِ اسْمِكَ وَبَلَدِكَ وَحَالِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-kharaja al-khādimu ilayhi wa-qāla lahu qul mā ʿindaka mina al-shiʿri fa-inna al-sitta ḥāḍiratun bi-al-qurbi minka tasmaʿuka wa-baʿda dhālika asʾaluka ʿan ismika wa-baladika wa-ḥālika
sentences.l: So the servant went out to him and said to him: Say what is with you of poetry, for the lady is present at the nearness of you, hearing you; and after that I ask you about your name and your country and your state.
sentences.i: So the servant went out to him and said, “Say whatever verses you have, for the lady is close by, listening to you; and after that I will ask you your name, your country, and how you are.”
sentences.n: The servant now speaks the lady’s words as his own: the “I” who asks is the servant relaying her question.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ حُبًّا وَكَرَامَةً وَلَكِنْ إِذَا سَأَلْتَنِي عَنِ اسْمِي فَإِنَّهُ مَحَا وَرَسْمِي فَنَى وَجِسْمِي بَلِيَ وَلِي حِكَايَةٌ لَا أَوَّلَ لَهَا يُعْرَفُ وَلَا آخِرَ لَهَا يُوصَفُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ḥubban wa-karāmatan wa-lākin idhā saʾaltanī ʿan ismī fa-innahu maḥā wa-rasmī fanā wa-jismī baliya wa-lī ḥikāyatun lā awwala lahā yuʿrafu wa-lā ākhira lahā yūṣafu
sentences.l: And he said: With love and honour; but if you ask me about my name — it has been effaced, and my trace has perished, and my body has worn away; and I have a story, no beginning of which is known, and no end of which is described,
sentences.i: He said, “With pleasure and honour. But if you ask me my name — it is effaced, my traces are gone, and my body is worn away. I have a story whose beginning cannot be known and whose end cannot be told,
sentences.n: حبا وكرامة is a courtesy formula of consent, “gladly and with honour”. محا is read as maḥā, “was effaced”, answering فنى and بلي in the rhymed run.

sentences.t: وَهَا أَنَا فِي مَنْزِلَةِ السَّكْرَانِ الَّذِي أَكْثَرَ مِنَ الشَّرَابِ وَمَا تَبَخَّلَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ وَحَلَّتْ بِهِ الْأَ وْصَابُ وَتَاهَ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ وَاحْتَارَ فِي أَمْرِهِ وَغَرِقَ فِي بَحْرِ الْأَ فْكَارِ
sentences.tr: wa-hā anā fī manzilati al-sakrāni alladhī akthara mina al-sharābi wa-mā tabakhkhala ʿalā nafsihi wa-ḥallat bihi al-aʾ awṣābu wa-tāha ʿan nafsihi wa-iḥtāra fī amrihi wa-ghariqa fī baḥri al-aʾ afkāri
sentences.l: and here I am in the station of the drunkard who has taken much of the drink and was not niggardly with himself, and the ailments have settled upon him, and he has strayed from himself, and been bewildered in his affair, and drowned in the sea of the thoughts.
sentences.i: and here I am, like a drunkard who has drunk deep and held nothing back from himself, upon whom sickness has settled; who has lost himself, is bewildered in his plight, and is drowned in a sea of thoughts.
sentences.n: The print splits الا وصاب and الا فكار after the article; the splits are kept. ما تبخل is read “he did not hold back” (a verb of the fifth form); the phrase is uncertain.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ نُزْهَةُ الزَّمَانِ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ بَكَتْ وَزَادَتْ فِى الْبُكَاءِ وَالْأَ نِينِ وَقَالَتْ لِلْخَادِمِ قُلْ لَهُ هَلْ فَارَقْتَ أَحَدًا مِمَّنْ تُحِبُّ مِثْلَ أُمِّكَ وَأَبِيكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat nuzhatu al-zamāni hādhā al-kalāma bakat wa-zādat fī al-bukāʾi wa-al-aʾ anīni wa-qālat li-al-khādimi qul lahu hal fāraqta aḥadan mimman tuḥibbu mithla ummika wa-abīka
sentences.l: And when Nuzhat al-Zamān heard this speech she wept, and increased in the weeping and the groaning, and said to the servant: Say to him: Have you parted from anyone of those you love, like your mother and your father?
sentences.i: When Nuzhat al-Zamān heard this she wept, and wept more and more, and sobbed. She said to the servant, “Ask him whether he has been parted from anyone he loves, such as his mother and his father.”

sentences.t: فَسَأَلَهُ الْخَادِمُ كَمَا أَمَرَتْهُ نُزْهَةُ الزَّمَانِ فَقَالَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ نَعَمْ فَارَقْتُ الْجَمِيعَ وَأَعَزُّهُمْ عِنْدِي أُخْتَى الَّتِي فَرَّقَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهَا الدَّهْرُ
sentences.tr: fa-saʾalahu al-khādimu kamā amarathu nuzhatu al-zamāni fa-qāla ḍawʾu al-makāni naʿam fāraqtu al-jamīʿa wa-aʿazzuhum ʿindī ukhtī allatī farraqa baynī wa-baynahā al-dahru
sentences.l: So the servant asked him as Nuzhat al-Zamān had commanded him, and Ḍawʾ al-Makān said: Yes, I have parted from all, and the dearest of them to me is my sister, between whom and me time has parted.
sentences.i: So the servant asked him as Nuzhat al-Zamān had told him, and Ḍawʾ al-Makān said, “Yes, I have been parted from all of them, and the dearest to me is my sister, whom time has torn from me.”
sentences.n: اختى is printed with a dotless final yāʾ (ى), as the edition often does; read as أختي.

sentences.t: فَسَكَتَتْ نُزْهَةُ الزَّمَانِ لَمَّا سَمِعَتْهُ يَقُولُ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ وَقَالَتْ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى يَجْمَعُ شَمْلَهُ بِمَنْ يُحِبُّ
sentences.tr: fa-sakatat nuzhatu al-zamāni lammā samiʿathu yaqūlu hādhā al-kalāma wa-qālat allāhu taʿālā yajmaʿu shamlahu bi-man yuḥibbu
sentences.l: And Nuzhat al-Zamān fell silent when she heard him say this speech, and said: God the Exalted gathers his union with the one he loves.
sentences.i: Nuzhat al-Zamān fell silent when she heard him say this, and said, “May God the Exalted gather him together again with the one he loves.”
sentences.n: The imperfect يجمع is read as a wish. بمن is “with the one whom”.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the speech the permitted.
sentences.i: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech unspoken.
sentences.n: The stock close of a night.
